campaign: Batch 32S PR #95/#96 file-backed mmap semantic review
observed_result: File-backed MAP_PRIVATE advanced real Alpine loader pressure and runtime rollback/ownership tests passed, but review found two Linux-semantic defects: plan() truncates copied bytes at EOF while retaining the full rounded requested mapping length, allowing wholly-past-EOF pages to become readable zero-filled mappings; and the planner accepts PROT_NONE/write-only protection shapes that the current Sv39 leaf encoder cannot represent cleanly, allowing late generic mapping failure instead of a deliberate compatibility policy
framework_assessment: Batch 32S explicitly required file-range validation, requested-permission semantics, deterministic errno, bounded failure atomicity, and Linux-compatible private mappings; no external limitation forced either defect; green CI did not cover these semantic gaps
corrective_action: Reject or leave unmapped pages wholly beyond EOF while only zero-filling the legitimate final partial file page; explicitly reject, reserve, or normalize PROT_NONE/write-only modes before mapping mutation; add focused regressions; retain current rollback/ownership and Playable Alpine proofs; keep the observed 950-page libcrypto backing-capacity requirement as the next causal frontier rather than mixing it into this cleanup
